newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says Megawati not on travel blacklist.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says Megawati not on travel blacklist.

text.p: Indonesian opposition figurehead Megawati Sukarnoputri has not been blacklisted or banned from travelling abroad, the official Antara news agency reported on Sunday.
"It's not true that Megawati has been blacklisted and she is free to go anywhere," director-general of immigration Pranowo was quoted as saying on Saturday.

Advisers to Megawati, former leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), said on Saturday that she had been briefly stopped at the immigration barrier on Saturday after a computer showed her listed as a banned person.
The advisers said after talking with officials and contacting her legal advisors Megawati was allowed to go Singapore with her family as officials had no written proof of the banning order.
They said Megawati was expected back in Jakarta on Sunday.
The Merdeka newspaper said on Sunday that Megawati had had a "war of words" with immigration officers after being told she was blacklisted and not allowed to travel abroad.

"I was surprised my name had been put on the blacklist. It is compulsory that if you are banned you are informed by the agency which is banning you but up to now I have not been told anything," Megawati was quoted as saying by Merdeka.
But Pranowo said Megawati had been processed using the same procedures as anyone else leaving the country.
"The examination was the usual thing which must be faced by all people. But what is clear is that the name Megawati Sukarnoputri has not been included on the blacklist," he said.

Megawati, ousted leader of the Indonesian Democractic Party (PDI), has been questioned three times by authorities since the July 27 riots in Jakarta which were sparked when police seized party headquarters from her loyalist supporters.
At least four people died and scores of buildings and vehicles were set ablaze in the riots, the worst in the capital in more than 20 years.
Megawati, the daughter of late founding president Sukarno, has become a symbol of dissent after she was ousted by a government-backed faction of the PDI in June.
